```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/helpers.R")
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

facilities <- load_facilities("data/facilities.yml")
raw_facs <- yaml::read_yaml("data/facilities.yml")$facilities
```

## The Global Node Landscape

Semiconductor "nodes" refer to manufacturing process technology; smaller numbers generally mean more advanced chips.

```{r node-chart, echo=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=7, dev="ragg_png"}
nodes <- tibble(
  node = c("3nm", "5nm", "7nm", "10nm", "14nm", "22nm", "28nm", "40nm", "55nm", "65nm", "90nm", "130nm", "180nm+"),
  node_nm = c(3, 5, 7, 10, 14, 22, 28, 40, 55, 65, 90, 130, 180),
  era = c("Cutting Edge", "Cutting Edge", "Advanced", "Advanced", "Advanced",
          "Mature", "Mature", "Mature", "Mature", "Legacy", "Legacy", "Legacy", "Legacy"),
  key_fabs = c(
    "TSMC, Samsung", "TSMC, Samsung", "TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SMIC (via SAQP)",
    "TSMC, Samsung, Intel", "TSMC, Samsung, Intel, SMIC", "Intel, GF, TSMC",
    "TSMC, Samsung, GF, SMIC, UMC, Hua Hong", "TSMC, UMC, SMIC, Hua Hong",
    "PSMC, UMC, Hua Hong", "Various (widely available)", "Various", "Various", "Various"
  )
)

era_colors <- c("Cutting Edge" = "#620d3c", "Advanced" = "#f1a222", "Mature" = "#2f6b6b", "Legacy" = "#8C8480")

ggplot(nodes, aes(x = reorder(node, -node_nm), y = 1, fill = era)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(node, ": ", key_fabs)), hjust = 0, nudge_y = 0.05, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = era_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 4)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Era") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
```

## China's Indigenization Trajectory

Each line traces one facility's most advanced disclosed process technology over time — the clearest signal of how effectively export controls have slowed (or failed to slow) specific fabs. **Logic/DRAM process width (nm) and 3D NAND layer count are different units and are never plotted on the same axis** — a higher layer count is more advanced, while a smaller nm figure is more advanced, so combining them on one chart would misread as a regression for exactly the facilities making the fastest progress.

```{r trajectory-chart, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=5, dev="ragg_png"}
trajectory_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(raw_facs, function(f) {
  if (is.null(f$node_trajectory) || length(f$node_trajectory) == 0) return(NULL)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(f$node_trajectory, function(t) {
    data.frame(facility = f$name_en, year = t$year, node = t$node, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))

# Strict unit-specific parsers: a value counts as an "nm" figure only when
# the string literally says "Nnm", and as a "layer" figure only when it
# literally says "N-layer" — never inferred from a bare leading number,
# which previously misread 3D NAND layer counts (e.g. "128-layer") as a
# 128nm process node.
node_to_nm <- function(s) {
  m <- regexpr("([0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?)\\s*nm", s, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)
  if (m[1] == -1) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", regmatches(s, m)))
}
node_to_layers <- function(s) {
  m <- regexpr("([0-9]+)-layer", s, ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE)
  if (m[1] == -1) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", regmatches(s, m)))
}

if (!is.null(trajectory_rows) && nrow(trajectory_rows) > 0) {
  trajectory_rows$node_nm <- sapply(trajectory_rows$node, node_to_nm)
  trajectory_rows$node_layers <- sapply(trajectory_rows$node, node_to_layers)
  nm_rows <- trajectory_rows[!is.na(trajectory_rows$node_nm), ]
  layer_rows <- trajectory_rows[!is.na(trajectory_rows$node_layers), ]
} else {
  nm_rows <- trajectory_rows[0, ]
  layer_rows <- trajectory_rows[0, ]
}
```

### Logic / DRAM Process Width

```{r nm-chart, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=4, dev="ragg_png"}
if (nrow(nm_rows) > 0) {
  ggplot(nm_rows, aes(x = year, y = node_nm, color = facility, group = facility)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    scale_y_reverse() +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Node (nm, smaller = more advanced)", color = "Facility") +
    theme_minimal()
} else {
  cat("*No nm-denominated node trajectory data yet.*")
}
```

### 3D NAND Layer Count

```{r layer-chart, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=4, dev="ragg_png"}
if (nrow(layer_rows) > 0) {
  ggplot(layer_rows, aes(x = year, y = node_layers, color = facility, group = facility)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 2) +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Layer count (higher = more advanced)", color = "Facility") +
    theme_minimal()
} else {
  cat("*No layer-count node trajectory data yet.*")
}
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading These Charts
A facility with no plotted line has not yet had its node history researched (see [About](about.qmd) for data status). Absence from a chart is a data gap, not a claim about the facility's capability. An entry whose process technology doesn't parse into either unit (for example, a named-but-unquantified node such as "DDR5-capable, exact width not disclosed") is excluded from both charts rather than guessed — it still appears in that facility's own profile page.
:::
